summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for confusion and a fall, with worsening back pain. He has a history of hepatitis C cirrhosis, recurrent hepatic encephalopathy, and prior vertebral osteomyelitis. Evaluation revealed hepatic encephalopathy likely triggered by pain and stress, with no evidence of acute infection. MRI showed new acute compression fractures at T9, T11, and L1, but no active osteomyelitis. A possible aortic valve vegetation seen on TTE was ruled out by TEE. He was treated with continued lactulose and rifaximin for encephalopathy, optimized diuretic therapy, and initiated on high-dose vitamin D and testosterone replacement for osteoporosis. A TLSO brace was fitted for spinal support. His mental status and pain improved, and he was discharged to extended care with follow-up plans.
